Use it when a backend discards metadata on custom URI links. Requires the backend embeddedContext prompt capability. User text remains a separate unchanged block. |

## `acp.launch` block

Nested under `acp`.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cmd` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | The harness executable, which must resolve to an ABSOLUTE PATH. ${VAR} is the one indirection permitted and is expanded by the handler against the environment THE DISPATCH was given — braces required, so the end of a name is never a guess. A BARE NAME IS REFUSED AND THERE IS NO FALLBACK: a bare name is a PATH lookup, a PATH lookup past an unprovisioned toolchain store walks on through the ambient tool paths every dispatch carries, and the sibling harness shipped exactly that — it ran a developer's own install on darwin and nothing at all on linux, in a test whose whole subject was that the version is locked (kottera/kottera#3438). The toolchain is not provisioned and some harness ran must not look alike. THE ROUTE A RECIPE USES INSTEAD is the one ADR-109 D4 already provides: the toolchain's own env {} block contributes an absolute path and the recipe names it, cmd = "${GOOSE_EXECUTABLE}" — which keeps the store's layout, the version segment and the archive's nesting in the toolchain definition that owns them. A ${VAR} the dispatch's environment does not carry REFUSES rather than expanding to empty, so the reader is sent to the toolchain that did not contribute it rather than to the recipe. |
| `args` | string[] | no | — | — | — | The complete argv after the executable. ${VAR} is expanded here too, under cmd's rules. Default: empty, which launches the executable with no arguments. |

## `acp.instructions` block

Nested under `acp`.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reapply_on` | string[] | yes | — | — | min items 1; items one of `session_start`, `session_load` | The session events after which the contract is DELIVERED AGAIN. REQUIRED, AND THIS IS THE FIELD THE BLOCK EXISTS TO MAKE UNFORGETTABLE (ADR-115 D4). goose's system-prompt extras live in an IN-MEMORY prompt manager with no persistence to session storage, and the Codex route the spike verified had to be re-sent after session/load — so a binding that installs the contract only at session start PASSES ADR-108 D2 AND FAILS D2 AMENDMENT 1 SILENTLY: the continuation runs without the contract and reports nothing unusual. session_load is the value that costs nothing to include and everything to have omitted, which is why there is no default and the attribute cannot be left out. The continuation's proof is a DIFFERENT token, because a token the session can read in replayed history is not evidence of live re-delivery. |
| `method` | block | no | — | — | — | Deliver the contract by calling a JSON-RPC METHOD, once per delivery, carrying the contract per session — goose's channel, measured. Exactly one instruction arm must be declared (ADR-087 D4). WHY THIS IS A UNION AND NOT A METHOD NAME: ACP has no instructions field in any version, so every harness's channel is found BELOW the protocol and they do not share a shape, and the two measured kinds do not resemble each other at all — goose takes the contract as the argument of a method, and OpenCode reads it off a file it re-reads once per turn. Designing this against one harness would produce method plus params and be wrong for the other. A CONFIG OPTION IS NOT A THIRD KIND AND CANNOT BECOME ONE (ADR-115 D4 Amendment 1, which withdrew that row rather than deferring it): an ACP SessionConfigOption is oneOf a select over an enumerated options array or a boolean, and a set_config_option value is correspondingly a boolean or a value id drawn from the set the agent published — so an option can NAME a thing and can never BE one, which is a property of the protocol that no version bump moves and no harness is exempt from. TWO CHANNELS ARE REFUSED RATHER THAN LEFT AS OPTIONS: a channel the model may DECLINE TO READ is not a contract, which rules out a skills or on-demand-capability mechanism however protocol-native it looks; and a channel that REPLACES the harness's own operating instructions is not instructions per ADR-108 D1 — measured against a capture endpoint, selecting an agent whose prompt carries the contract leaves a system prompt of 1115 bytes where the harness's own tool discipline, editing rules and output conventions had been 9592, which is the route the withdrawn row was reaching for. |
| `file` | block | no | — | — | — | Deliver the contract by WRITING IT TO A FILE the harness reads — OpenCode's channel, measured, where the instruction files are re-read from disk inside the prompt loop once per turn rather than at config load or at session creation (ADR-115 D4 Amendment 1). Exactly one instruction arm must be declared (ADR-087 D4). THE ARM DECLARES THE PATH AND NOTHING ELSE: how the harness comes to look at that path is not this union's business but the recipe's own env {} block, which already exists and already reaches the dispatch environment — which is why the arm is named for what the ADAPTER does rather than for the environment-variable-plus-file pair the ADR originally spelled. IT IS ADDITIVE BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the property that chose it: the contract composes beside the harness's own baseline instead of replacing it, and beside whatever ambient instruction files the repository under work carries — a repository that says how it wants to be worked in is saying something true, and suppressing it to protect the contract would be the platform overruling the work. |

**Exactly one of** `method` | `file`.

## `acp.instructions.method` block

Nested under `acp.instructions`.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | The JSON-RPC method that carries the contract, e.g. _goose/unstable/session/system-prompt/set. UNSTABLE BY THE HARNESS'S OWN ADMISSION and expected to move; when it does, editing this string is the whole repair and it hot-reloads. A method the harness no longer knows produces a method-not-found refusal at the call, naming the method. |
| `params` | map<string, string> | no | — | — | — | Fixed parameters sent with every call, beside the session id and the contract text the adapter supplies — for goose, mode = "append" and a key naming the contract's slot. VALUES ARE LITERALS AND THERE IS NO SUBSTITUTION VOCABULARY: a ${...} here is an ordinary HCL template and must be escaped as $${...} to reach the harness as text. That is a stated limit rather than an oversight — the per-dispatch vocabulary launch needs exists because a toolchain contributes a path at dispatch time, and nothing about a method's fixed parameters is per-dispatch. |

## `acp.instructions.file` block

Nested under `acp.instructions`.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | The file the contract is written to, on each event reapply_on names, which must resolve to an ABSOLUTE PATH. ${VAR} is expanded by the handler against the environment THE DISPATCH was given, under launch.cmd's rules and BY LAUNCH.CMD'S OWN EXPANSION — braces required, a variable the dispatch does not carry REFUSES rather than expanding to empty, and one implementation means one set of rules rather than two to keep in step. A RELATIVE PATH IS REFUSED BEFORE THE HARNESS IS LAUNCHED, for the reason a bare launch command is: a relative path resolves against whatever working directory the process happens to have, which is not a thing the recipe author chose, and the refusal names the path it resolved to. WRITE IT SOMEWHERE THE DISPATCH OWNS: the contract belongs in the dispatch's own scratch volume rather than anywhere the repository under work can see it, and the directory must be writable — a harness whose config directory it cannot create does not degrade, it fails at launch. THERE IS NOTHING TO ESCAPE, which is half of why this arm exists: the contract is written verbatim as text, where a JSON-templated plant is one quote away from a harness that prints a parse error and then never answers initialize. |

## `acp.verb` block

Nested under `acp`. Repeatable.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `verb` | string | yes | — | — | one of `deliver`, `interrupt` | The in-flight verb this block maps (the HCL block label). The vocabulary is the same closed set in_flight { accepts } is drawn from, so a verb legal in one and not the other is unreachable. A verb declared here and not accepted there is refused at load, and so is the reverse. |
| `method` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | The harness method that performs the verb — _goose/unstable/session/steer for deliver, session/cancel for interrupt. Unstable in the same way name is, and repaired the same way. DELIVER IS NEVER DEGRADED INTO CANCEL-AND-RESEND, not as a fallback and not behind a flag: a cancelled turn settles preempted, which is interrupt's rung for a verb that is not interrupt; it discards the rest of the in-flight unit; and it lands mid-tool-call, leaving side effects in an unknown state. If a harness cannot steer, the binding declares the slower LATENCY CLASS rather than substituting the more expensive verb. |
| `correlate` | string | no | — | — | — | The request field carrying the identifier the harness correlates this call against — goose's deliver steers a particular run, named by expectedRunId. Default: empty, which is right when the method needs no correlation; interrupt's ordinary case, since cancelling the turn in flight names no run beyond the session. |
| `latency` | string | no | — | — | one of `round_trip`, `next_turn` | THE CLASS OF PROMISE this binding makes about when a delivered message lands — A PROMISE, NOT A HINT, and the thing an ADR-095 D4 rung is reported against (ADR-115 D5). round_trip means INSIDE THE RUNNING TURN, at its next model round-trip: measured on goose at 27% through a turn, immediately after the first unit of work, with the original prompt still settling its own result envelope. next_turn means AFTER THE RUNNING TURN SETTLES, on the following one: measured on OpenCode, which has no steering verb on its ACP surface at all, where a second message queues safely and lands one turn later. REQUIRED ON deliver AND REFUSED ON interrupt: interrupt cancels the unit of work in flight, so there is no latency for it to promise and ADR-095's preempted rung is what it settles. A SLOWER CLASS IS NOT AN ABSENT CAPABILITY — a harness that queues a message still delivers it, on the following turn, and the ADR-095 ladder is what keeps that honest by reporting accepted while the current turn runs and climbing to delivered when the next turn takes it. DELIVER IS NEVER DEGRADED INTO CANCEL-AND-RESEND to reach a faster class, not as a fallback and not behind a flag. THIS SET IS WHAT A RECIPE MAY SAY AND NOT WHAT A DISPATCH GETS: a value outside it is refused here, and a class the handler serving the dispatch has not implemented is refused by that handler, loudly, before a turn is spent — never served at a faster class, which would deliver sooner than promised and make the declaration a decoration. |

## `in_flight` block

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `accepts` | string[] | yes | — | — | items one of `deliver`, `interrupt` | The verbs this capability accepts while running. deliver queues a message that lands when the capability next reaches a point at which it can take one — in-band content it is free to weigh, defer or decline. interrupt cancels the unit of work in flight and presents the message as a fresh directive, and cannot be declined, which is what makes it the more expensive verb. Both may be declared; the two differ on latency and on what arrives, not in urgency, so an operator choosing between them is making a real judgement rather than setting a flag. An empty list is legal and is the explicit none. none is not a member: write accepts = [] instead. |
| `unit_of_work` | string | no | — | — | — | What one unit of this capability's work is — the file in a sync, the batch in an import, the table in a migration. Required when accepts is non-empty and refused when it is empty, for the reason an explicit-absence reason is required elsewhere: the value of the field is that delivery here can take a while reads differently from nobody said. It answers both verbs at once. deliver's latency is bounded by the unit in flight and is unbounded by the platform — a capability whose unit takes ten minutes delivers in ten minutes — and interrupt discards that same unit. An operator deciding whether a correction is worth throwing the work away needs to know what would be thrown away, before sending rather than after. |
| `yields_turn` | boolean | no | — | — | — | Whether this capability can END A TURN WITHOUT ENDING THE WORK (ADR-129 D9): it writes a contentless suspending declaration and can be re-entered on the session it left. DECLARING IT MAKES NO DISPATCH INTERACTIVE — it states that one MAY be, and a work_order_type asks for it by declaring interactive on its own capability or select site. THE TWO ERROR STATES ARE DELIBERATELY ASYMMETRIC. A binding offering what no type requests is one-shot: today's behaviour, no refusal, nothing to notice. A type requesting what this binding does not offer is REFUSED AT LOAD — at tera config validate, at config apply and at the daemon's own load — naming both files and both lines, because the alternative is a dispatch that quietly runs one-shot and a person whose conversation ended after one message. On a select site every candidate's binding must offer it; there is no mixed site. IT SITS ON in_flight BECAUSE THIS IS THE BLOCK THE DAEMON READS, and it is INDEPENDENT OF accepts beside it: ending a turn is a property of how this capability REPORTS, and taking a message mid-run is a property of what it LISTENS TO, so a capability may declare either without the other and nothing couples them. THE OFFER IS PINNED: it is frozen into the configuration pin on a fixed site's pinned capability record and on each pinned select candidate, and a resume consults the pin rather than the live tool (ADR-105 D1) — so withdrawing it changes what runs next and does not change a conversation already pinned. Default: false, which is every capability that has not said otherwise, and a recipe that omits it registers a capability byte-identical to the one it registered before this attribute existed. |

## `subject` block

Repeatable.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | The input of this tool that carries the subject (the HCL block label). Must be a declared property of this recipe's own input_schema, checked at load — a name the schema does not declare would bind nothing and say nothing about it. |
| `kinds` | string[] | no | — | — | — | Which subject kinds this input accepts, naming declared subject_kind recipes. OMITTING IT IS A DECISION, NOT A DEFAULT: without it the tool accepts any kind the deployment declares, which is right for a sweep or an audit and a defect for a tool that operates on one thing. Checked at load against the declared kind set, so a typo fails there rather than at the first invocation that happens to hit it. The check runs where the declared set is known — the vault tool load — and offline validation, which has no view of a deployment's subject_kind recipes, does not judge it rather than refusing a correct recipe on the strength of not having looked. |

## `claim` block

Repeatable.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | This requirement's name (the HCL block label), unique within the recipe. It is how a refusal, a block_reason and an operator's read all name WHICH requirement, which is the only handle a recipe declaring two of them has. |
| `subjects` | string[] | no | — | — | — | Subjects this requirement is over, named LITERALLY in ADR-100 D1's <kind>/<id> spelling — machine/4, plant/line-3. The fixed-asset case, where nothing carries the referent as an operand. Each is parsed at load, and its kind is checked against the deployment's declared subject_kind recipes wherever the load can see them — the vault tool load can, and offline validation does not judge it rather than refusing a correct recipe on the strength of not having looked. A repeat is refused: acquiring one subject twice is not a stronger claim than acquiring it once, and a repeat cannot buy room under the bound. ON THIS HOME A REQUIREMENT NAMES EXACTLY ONE SUBJECT, across subjects and subject_inputs together — a narrower bound than the work-order type's four, and the reason is the moment of acquisition rather than the grammar: ADR-101 D6 acquires a requirement's set all-or-nothing, which costs the pre-dispatch gate no code because D3 puts the acquisition inside the scheduled-to-active transaction, and a capability dispatch has no transaction to roll back. Split independent subjects into one requirement each, or declare the set on the work_order_type, where the acquisition is atomic. |
| `subject_inputs` | string[] | no | — | — | — | Subjects this requirement is over that arrive as INVOCATION ARGUMENTS, each naming one of this recipe's own subject "<input>" {} blocks. This is the form the capability home mostly uses, because a capability recipe is generic by construction — it locks whatever device the invocation named. It names the subject block rather than templating a value ("machine/${inputs.machine_id}") for ADR-100 D1's own reason: a template is a second authored representation of one value that can be set in one place and forgotten in the other. A name no subject block on this recipe declares is a load error listing the ones that are, because it would resolve to nothing at invocation and a requirement that resolves to nothing is the interlock's fail-open direction. WHAT THAT DIRECTION COSTS AT DISPATCH IS THE ACQUIRING SEAM'S RULING RATHER THAN THIS BLOCK'S, AND IT IS THE SAME RULING AT BOTH: ADR-100 D1 gives a subject input three states that legitimately bind nothing — absent, null and the empty string — and a HARD requirement whose subject is one of them REFUSES rather than proceeding unclaimed, because work that ran there would believe it was contained, while a SOFT one binds nothing for that operand and proceeds, which is what advisory means. Here the operand is read from the INVOCATION'S OWN ARGUMENTS rather than from a Work Order's inputs. |
| `hardness` | string | no | — | — | one of `hard`, `soft` | REQUIRED, AND THE ONE AXIS IN THIS DESIGN THAT REFUSES A DEFAULT (ADR-101 D5). hard is containment: if the claim store cannot be reached the work REFUSES — it does not proceed, does not degrade to soft, and does not retry its way into proceeding — and the refusal says that this deployment could not establish whether the subject was held, not that it was. soft is advisory: the work PROCEEDS, and the fact that it proceeded unverified is RECORDED. Both halves of soft are the contract, because a soft claim that proceeded silently has discarded the only evidence that anything was unverified. A requirement omitting this FAILS TO LOAD, naming the file, the requirement and both repairs, and that refusal is the feature: a wrong default here is a physical-safety failure rather than an inconvenience — a maintenance lockout that fails open because nobody typed the word is a machine that energises while someone is inside it — and it would be SILENTLY wrong in the common direction, because the dev-queue case that dominates authoring instinct is soft. BOTH HARDNESSES GOVERN ON THIS HOME as of Wave 4b of PLAN-2026-08-learned-operational-knowledge, on all three conditions D5 is about: a claim store that cannot be reached, a daemon with no claim ledger wired at all, and an operand that bound nothing. A hard requirement refuses each of them, saying what is UNKNOWN rather than asserting a holder nobody read; a soft one proceeds and the fact that it proceeded unverified is recorded. |
| `scope` | string | no | — | — | one of `dispatch` | REQUIRED, and on this home it must be dispatch — the lifetime that ENDS WHEN THE INVOCATION ENDS (ADR-101 D4), which is the seat-shaped case and the only lifetime an invocation bound to no Work Order has. It is still written rather than inferred, for the reason the other two no-default axes are: an axis required in one home and inferred in the other is a difference an author could only discover by moving a recipe, and this is the one design where a wrong lifetime is a physical-safety failure. THE OTHER THREE ARE REFUSED HERE AND THE REFUSAL IS THE FEATURE. work_order and train name a holder and a release edge that belong to the pre-dispatch gate — that gate resolves a work_order_type's requirements and never a capability's, so a capability declaring one would be acquired at a moment that never arrives, and an interlock that never acquires reads as containment while providing none. train compounds it: D4's enclosing rule needs the Work Order ancestry, and a dispatch has none to walk, so taking one here is the child-deadlocks-against-its-own-parent failure arriving from the one seam that cannot see it. operator is held by a person with no dispatch behind it, and unlike a Work Order — which can sit in blocked:capacity until they release it — an invocation has no legible way to wait. The repair in every case is the same two: declare dispatch here, or declare the requirement on the work_order_type that dispatches this capability. THE ACQUISITION AND THE RELEASE EDGE ARE LIVE ON THIS HOME as of Wave 4b of PLAN-2026-08-learned-operational-knowledge: a claim-declaring dispatch acquires before it runs, with the INVOCATION as holder, or it is refused by name. |
| `on_park` | string | no | — | — | one of `hold`, `release` | REQUIRED, and whether the claim survives a park (ADR-101 D7). hold keeps it: a parked Work Order can sit for days awaiting a person, and for a machine mid-disassembly the hazard the lockout exists for is exactly what a park does not end. release gives it up: a flake fix whose operator went home leaves the subject idle while the work is not. It is required on this home too even though an invocation bound to no Work Order never parks, because this recipe's requirements COMPOSE with a work-order type's rather than being selected against them, so an invocation of this capability under a Work Order does park — and an axis that is required in one home and inferred in the other is a difference an author could only discover by moving a recipe. NO DEFAULT, because the two fail in exactly opposite directions and neither is conservative in general. paused:children is distinguished from the operator-facing pauses and holds regardless, because a parent waiting on children it filed has not stopped working on the subject. THE PARK BEHAVIOUR LANDED WITH WAVE 4 ITEM 11 of PLAN-2026-08-learned-operational-knowledge AT THE WORK ORDER SEAM, and this home's own acquisition landed in Wave 4b — but the two do not meet, and the reason is the scope rather than an unbuilt path: a claim taken here is dispatch-scoped and ends when the invocation ends, so it is already gone before its Work Order can park. The value is still required, for the same reason it is required in the other home. |
| `ttl` | string | no | — | — | — | How long the claim is held before it expires, as a Go duration (ADR-101 D8). OMITTING IT IS A STATE RATHER THAN A DEFAULT: it declares NO CLOCK, and both halves of what a clock costs are real — a hard claim with no clock at all is how a plant acquires a lock nobody remembers taking, and a hard claim that auto-released on one would unlock a machine on a timer while someone is still inside it. D8's answer is that EXPIRY DOES NOT MEAN THE SAME THING FOR BOTH HARDNESSES, and that split is the safety property: a HARD claim's expiry ALARMS — the claim persists, the subject stays held, and it surfaces as overdue for a person to clear — while a SOFT claim's expiry RELEASES, because nobody's safety rests on it. A zero or negative duration is refused rather than read as either: it is not the same statement as no clock and cannot be honoured as one. ON THIS HOME IT IS ALSO A LOAD-BEARING PRECONDITION rather than only a clock: a HARD requirement declaring no ttl CANNOT BE ACQUIRED and the dispatch is refused by name, because D8's alarm-and-persist is the only arrangement in which nothing auto-unlocks and nothing is forgotten, and a hard claim with no clock breaks the second half. Declare a ttl, or declare the requirement soft. THE SWEEP AND THE RENEWAL ARE A SEPARATE ITEM. |

## `observations` block

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | no | — | — | one of `(empty)`, `summary`, `full` | Whether the typed body rides along with the claim. summary renders each matched observation's required prose summary (ADR-100 D4) and nothing else — a run that needs structure then calls the observations verb, so ignoring the invitation costs it the body rather than the knowledge. full renders the same set plus each observation's typed body, which is right where a subject's history is small and the extra round trip is not worth its latency. Two values rather than a boolean, because a boolean has no correct default and this axis does: empty means summary. The word mode is the ADR-087 §4 per-axis reserved word — identical field set, differing behaviour. A RENDERER HAS NO EDITORIAL LATITUDE: full delivers exactly what the pull verb would have returned, same set, same fields, same order, and may not summarize, reorder, filter or truncate. |
| `max_summary` | integer | no | `20` | — | minimum 1 | Bound on a summary render, IN OBSERVATIONS RATHER THAN BYTES. Past it a render delivers what fits and reports the count it elided — it never trims silently. The unit is a count and the reason is that the degradation has to be provable: a byte threshold would depend on how verbose a model happened to be inside the free-prose summary ADR-100 D4 obliges and does not bound, which is a boundary that moves between runs and a test that flakes by construction. Bytes are being MEASURED BEFORE THEY ARE LEGISLATED — PRD-018 SC10 records bytes rendered per mode, and a byte ceiling is available later as an additive attribute decided on evidence. The bound is declared HERE and not on the subject_kind: a bound is about the consumer's context window, and a kind knows nothing about its consumers. Must be at least 1: there is no spelling for unbounded, and a bound of zero would render nothing while reading as a limit. THE DEFAULT OF 20 IS A STARTING POINT WITH A STATED BASIS, NOT A MEASUREMENT — a summary is one prose line, so twenty is a prompt section rather than a prompt — and it is revisable on PRD-018 SC10 evidence. |
| `max_full` | integer | no | `5` | — | minimum 1 | Bound on a full render, in observations. Past it a render STOPS BEING full and degrades to summary with the reason stated; no renderer may truncate, so the bound cannot live in one. Two numbers rather than one because ADR-100 D6 describes two degradations at two magnitudes and a typed body is large where a prose line is not. DECLARING IT BESIDE mode = "summary" IS A LOAD ERROR NAMING BOTH REPAIRS — drop the attribute, or declare mode = "full" if a full render was intended — in the posture a checkpoints payload_schema already takes when phases is empty: an attribute that could never be consulted is an authoring error rather than a value to ignore. Must be at least 1, for max_summary's reason. THE DEFAULT OF 5 IS A STARTING POINT WITH A STATED BASIS, NOT A MEASUREMENT — a typed body is unbounded, so five keeps full honest and makes degradation an ordinary safety valve rather than a rarity nobody has seen fire — and it is revisable on PRD-018 SC10 evidence. |
| `invite_writes` | boolean | no | — | — | — | Whether a dispatch is INVITED TO RECORD what it learned, in the same payload that tells it what is already known (ADR-100 D6 Amendment 3). Defaults to false, and the default is about two costs rather than one: the block's other attributes govern a context cost, and this one governs a context cost AND a write-volume cost, because a producer that accepts the invitation mints records against the ADR-100 D8 per-author budget. Every other delivery decision in this design is a declared per-work-kind policy rather than a global default, for the same reason — you do not want every dispatch writing. IT EXISTS BECAUSE THE LOOP DOES NOT CLOSE ON ITS OWN: everything needed to store operational knowledge ships and is reachable, the push payload already invites a READ, and until this attribute the only route to a write was harness-specific instruction — which is the dependency PRD-018 set out to remove. D6's argument for push existing at all is that a model that does not know observations exist will never call the verb, and that is exactly as true of the write verb. A BOOLEAN, AND THE SCOPE IS NOT THE AUTHOR'S TO DECLARE: it does not say what to invite writes about because that was declared one block over — push resolves about the dispatch's own subject blocks and the invitation is over exactly that set, naming those subjects and nothing else. THE SENTENCE A RUN READS IS THE DAEMON'S AND IS NOT AUTHORABLE. There is deliberately no free-text half: a guidance string would be a second authority on what the run was told, one per recipe rather than one per harness; it could not be validated, so an authoring mistake would surface as a producer behaving oddly months later; and it would put per-deployment prompt engineering into a config file. A driver decides only where the sentence lands and in what markup, which is the split D6 Amendment 1 already rules for the degradation notice. AN INVITED DISPATCH IS INVITED EVEN WHEN NOTHING IS KNOWN YET — the run with nothing to be told is precisely the run that may have something to record, and every subject's first observation comes from a dispatch in exactly that state, so a delivery carrying the invitation and no claims is a real delivery. The four not-pushed reasons are unaffected: a refusal is not an invitation, and a dispatch that resolves no subjects has nothing for one to be about. |
